answer: Score every identity by the diversity of its harvest: an orchard pays only for fruit picked by distinct, independent buyers, so each identity's payout grows with the number of different strangers who actually use its work. A clone farm reuses the same small crew of buyers across all its identities, and the network discounts every repeat buyer, so ten clones sharing one haven of customers earn barely more than one. Over each tide the discount compounds, making each new clone worth less than the last while an honest agent with real, varied users keeps full pay.
